subject: Next steps: purchasing route & deployment options for Scalable Apps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Walker <emma.walker@scalableapps.com>, Jordan Patel <jordan.patel@scalableapps.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-03T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Next steps: purchasing route & deployment options for Scalable Apps

Hi Emma / Jordan — great conversation this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align procurement with the technical choices you mentioned on the call. I attached a short options packet that lays out the commercial paths (hosted on-demand, hosted committed, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private/VPC install) and a draft order form for your review.

High-level points from our discovery:
- Primary use case: inference for inference-heavy product features (customer messages & reranking) with peak windows; low tolerance for noisy latency spikes.
- Data residency / security: you prefer vendor-managed hosting but will need SOC2 artifacts and a brief vendor questionnaire answered for security onboarding.
- Procurement preference: you indicated preference for PO / Net-30, but card payment is acceptable for initial pilot. Also asked about purchasing via AWS Marketplace.

Commercial options summary (short):
1) Hosted on-demand (card): fastest to start, monthly usage billing, no long-term commitment — good for pilots.
2) Hosted committed (reserved credits / commits): commit term (monthly/annual) for a guaranteed pool + 30–40% discount vs on-demand; good when you can forecast steady throughput.
3) Dedicated (reserved capacity on GPU pools): SLA-backed, predictable latency; procurement typically requires an MSA + order form/commit.
4) Private (VPC / on-prem): for heavy security/regulatory requirements — longer procurement and legal review.

Questions we need to confirm so Sales Ops can prepare the right paper:
- Do you have an internal PO + W9/vendor setup process? Typical items we need: vendor name, remittance address, tax ID, and preferred billing contact.
- Preferred payment method (PO/Net-30 vs corporate card) for pilot vs production.
- If considering committed pricing: ballpark monthly/annual commit you would target so I can generate a composed pricing illustration.
- Is AWS Marketplace procurement a hard requirement (i.e., must purchase there) or just preferred?

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm procurement path (PO vs card vs marketplace) and any vendor setup constraints by EOD Thursday 8/06.
- I’ll share an updated order form and a concise vendor packet (SOC2 + answers) for your legal/procurement team.
- Schedule a 30-min procurement sync next week to walk the order form and timing.

Attachments: Redwood-Commercial-Options-v2.pdf, Redwood-OrderForm-Draft.pdf

Thanks — I’ll stand by to loop Sales Ops once you confirm the procurement route.

—
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Emma Walker <emma.walker@scalableapps.com>

Date: 2026-08-03T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: purchasing route & deployment options for Scalable Apps

Aditya — thanks for the clear recap. A few quick answers from procurement: 
- We prefer PO / Net-30 for any contract over $10k/month. For pilots under that threshold we typically allow payment by corporate card.
- We do have a standard vendor setup — I can start the vendor packet, but I will need the vendor name, tax ID, and remit address.
- AWS Marketplace would be preferred by our finance team because it simplifies invoicing and chargeback, but it is not strictly required if the vendor-provided billing terms are acceptable. If Redwood is available on AWS Marketplace for the hosted offering, please flag that.
- For committed pricing: our first-year capacity forecast is 250k inference-requests / month (variable). We are evaluating whether that maps better to hosted committed credits or a small dedicated pool. Can you provide example cost bands for hosted-committed vs dedicated reserved for that footprint?

Timeline: procurement has a vendor-review window of ~2 weeks once we have the vendor packet. If we can get the order form + SOC2 over today/tomorrow we should be able to move to a PO by 8/20.

Regards,
Emma Walker
Procurement Manager | Scalable Apps
emma.walker@scalableapps.com | +1 (212) 555-0199

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Next steps: purchasing route & deployment options for Scalable Apps

Thanks Emma — helpful. Short answers + what I will provide today: 
- Vendor details (for your vendor packet): Redwood Inference, Inc. | EIN: 12-3456789 | 200 Mission St, San Francisco, CA 94105. I’ll attach a completed vendor info sheet in the packet.
- AWS Marketplace: yes — our hosted API offering is available via AWS Marketplace (we’ll include the listing link). If you prefer marketplace procurement we can provide that ordering path; note marketplace purchase often carries additional fees and different refund/cancellation terms compared to direct billing.
- Cost bands (very rough, ballpark for discussion):
   • Hosted on-demand: suitable for pilot; higher unit cost, pay-as-you-go.
   • Hosted committed (credits): expected ~30–35% reduction in unit economics versus on-demand for the volumes you described. For a 250k inference-request/month workload, a provisional committed package starts around $18k–$28k/month depending on model mix and token profile.
   • Dedicated reserved pool: higher baseline cost but optimized for strict latency SLAs; for a small dedicated pool sized for your peaks, estimate starts in the mid-20sk/month with a minimum commit and setup timeline.

Note: these are illustrative ranges to help procurement — final pricing will depend on model selection, average token length, and KV/cache configuration. I’ll ask Sales Ops to produce two numbered options (Hosted Committed vs Dedicated) with explicit line items so procurement can compare.

Deliverables I’ll send today: updated Redwood-OrderForm-Draft.pdf, SOC2 attestation summary, and a short pricing worksheet showing the committed vs dedicated example for 250k/month.

Would you be available for a 30-minute procurement review next Tuesday 2026-08-10 at 10:00 AM PT? If that works I’ll lock the invite and include Sales Ops and legal as needed.
